A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSGM study, and all ten pages of each, including equations, figures and tables, are readable. Neither contains appendices or embedded supplements; separately referenced supplementary material is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, image-generation evaluations, downstream inpainting and reconstruction results, and optimization ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Stable Diffusion experiments on Imagenette, including a pseudo-label sensitivity comparison.

M1.justification: The Orthogonal-MSGM and Obtuse-MSGM objectives, combined loss and alternating update procedure remain unchanged. Stable Diffusion is evaluated as another application of MSGM without introducing a new algorithmic component or objective.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates four image datasets through unconditional class/attribute unlearning and downstream tasks. v2 retains this coverage and adds high-resolution Imagenette with text-conditioned forgetting of the 'tench' class, substantially extending the input and task coverage.

E2.justification: ESD becomes an evaluated comparator in the new text-to-image experiment, having previously only been cited. EraseDiff also gains comparisons on STL-10 and CelebA in Table 2 and fine-tuned CelebA in v2 Table 3, where v1 reported no entries.

E3.justification: The added experiment uses SD v1.4 cross-attention fine-tuning and classification rate on images conditioned on the forgotten class. Existing protocols retain 10,000-image UR evaluation, the stated fine-tuning budgets, inpainting masks and reconstruction time t = 0.02.

E4.justification: v2 Section 4.4 and Figure 6 add a targeted sensitivity test using the semantically related pseudo-label 'cyprinoid' when forgetting 'tench'. The existing loss-weight and simultaneous-versus-alternating-update ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added results use the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Imagenette results give FID/CR of 3.08/0.00 for MSGM, 3.09/0.00 for both ESD and EraseDiff, and 4.89/0.74 for SD v1.4 (v2 Table 5). v2 also reports EraseDiff CR 0.47 with 'cyprinoid' and adds EraseDiff URs of 2.6% on STL-10, 1.2% on CelebA and 1.9% on fine-tuned CelebA. Matched pre-existing numerical entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SDE formulation, score-matching objectives and orthogonality/negative-inner-product conditions are retained. Replacing 'null space' with 'orthogonal complement space' and rewriting the loss notation clarify existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central claims about MSGM and shortcomings of retraining remain. v2 expands demonstrated applicability to conditional text-to-image generation and latent diffusion, whereas v1's conclusion listed text conditioning and high-resolution extensions as future work.

C2.justification: v2 introduces the interpretation that semantically similar pseudo-labels undermine forgetting and that MSGM avoids this dependence. It also removes v1 Section 4.1's explicit caveat about whole-distribution quality metrics when forgotten content is replaced with noise.

D1.justification: v2 specifies SD v1.4, cross-attention fine-tuning and pseudo-label choices for the added experiments. Existing optimization details remain, and both versions still promise code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Fastai and latent-diffusion references and removes the surveys by Na Li et al. and Tao Wang et al. It adds positioning around pseudo-label-free conditional unlearning, while the main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract and introduction, revises selected motivation and experimental-setup passages, corrects terminology and renames Section 3.3. It moves DDPM fine-tuning before downstream applications; the overall structure and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5–6 and Table 5 for conditional generation and substantially rearranges the experimental displays. Existing inpainting examples are transposed, reconstruction panels are reduced and resized, and several tables move alongside their reordered sections.

improvement.justification: The added SD/Imagenette comparison and pseudo-label sensitivity test support an application v1 left to future work, while additional EraseDiff scores improve comparative coverage. The gains are limited by evaluation of one forgotten class, absent uncertainty for the tiny FID advantage, and removal of a useful quality-evaluation caveat.
